Now only the `offer_editor` role can change offers, on the page and on the server. Format, lint, typecheck and the full test suite pass (1552 tests, 90.6% coverage). I didn't check it in the running app.

- **Server:** `can_edit_offers` in [access.py](components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/access.py) now only checks for the `offer_editor` role. `@requires_offer_editor` uses it, so every save handler refuses everyone else, admins included, with the usual "no permission" message.
- **Page:** this already matched. The buttons and fields check the role through appkit's `requires_role`.
- **Reading:** still open to every signed-in user.
- **Tests:** the offer state tests now act as an offer editor instead of an admin. A new test checks that an admin without the role can't create an offer.

To edit offers, an admin now has to give themselves the `offer_editor` role on the user page.

The planning Gantt files still have uncommitted changes that aren't from me. They should stay out of the offers commit.

"""Access levels of the alloq roles next to appkit's admin rights.

Admins may do everything. Project managers may read and edit every planning
page; the administration pages stay admin-only (``@requires_admin``). Users
with the employee role may only read the projects and planning pages. Every
signed-in user may read the offers; only the offer editor role may change
them, admins included.
"""

import inspect
import logging
from collections.abc import Callable
from functools import wraps
from typing import Any, Final

import reflex as rx

import appkit_mantine as mn
from alloq_commons.roles import EMPLOYEE_ROLE, OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE, PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE
from appkit_user.authentication.backend.models import User
from appkit_user.authentication.states import LoginState, UserSession

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_NOT_AUTHORIZED_MSG: Final = "Sie haben keine Berechtigung für diese Aktion."

ACCESS_LEVEL_ATTR: Final = "alloq_access_level"
"""Attribute naming the guard (``viewer``/``editor``) of a decorated handler."""

IS_ADMIN: Final = UserSession.user.is_admin
"""Frontend Var: the signed-in user is an admin."""
CAN_EDIT: Final = IS_ADMIN | UserSession.user.roles.contains(PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE.name)
"""Frontend Var: the signed-in user may read and edit the planning pages."""
CAN_VIEW: Final = CAN_EDIT | UserSession.user.roles.contains(EMPLOYEE_ROLE.name)
"""Frontend Var: the signed-in user may read projects and planning."""


def can_edit(user: User) -> bool:
    """Whether ``user`` may read and edit the planning pages."""
    return user.is_admin or PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE.name in user.roles


def can_view(user: User) -> bool:
    """Whether ``user`` may read the projects and planning pages."""
    return can_edit(user) or EMPLOYEE_ROLE.name in user.roles


def can_edit_offers(user: User) -> bool:
    """Whether ``user`` may edit offers; only the offer editor role may."""
    return OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE.name in user.roles


NO_ACCESS_MSG: Final = (
    "Sie haben nicht die notwendigen Berechtigungen, um auf diese Seite zuzugreifen."
)


def no_access() -> rx.Component:
    """Page content for signed-in users without read access."""
    return mn.center(
        mn.stack(
            mn.text(NO_ACCESS_MSG, fz="15px", fw=500),
            rx.link("Zu den Angeboten", href="/offers"),
            align="center",
            gap=8,
        ),
        h="60vh",
        px=24,
    )


def viewer_only(*children: Any, fallback: rx.Component | None = None) -> rx.Component:
    """Render ``children`` for admins, project managers and employees."""
    return rx.cond(CAN_VIEW, rx.fragment(*children), fallback)


def editor_only(*children: Any, fallback: rx.Component | None = None) -> rx.Component:
    """Render ``children`` for admins and project managers (edit controls)."""
    return rx.cond(CAN_EDIT, rx.fragment(*children), fallback)


def admin_only(*children: Any, fallback: rx.Component | None = None) -> rx.Component:
    """Render ``children`` for admins only (administration)."""
    return rx.cond(IS_ADMIN, rx.fragment(*children), fallback)


def _guard[F: Callable[..., Any]](
    func: F, allowed: Callable[[User], bool], level: str
) -> F:
    """Wrap event handler ``func`` so only users passing ``allowed`` run it.

    Mirrors appkit's ``requires_admin``: unauthenticated callers are redirected
    to login, everyone else without the right gets a permission error.
    """

    async def _check(self: Any) -> tuple[bool, Any]:
        """``(allowed, event)``; ``event`` answers a denied call."""
        login_state = await self.get_state(LoginState)
        user = await login_state.authenticated_user
        if user is None:
            logger.debug("User not authenticated, redirecting to login.")
            return False, await login_state.redir()
        if not allowed(user):
            logger.warning(
                "User user_id=%s denied %s action '%s'",
                user.user_id,
                level,
                func.__name__,
            )
            return False, rx.toast.error(_NOT_AUTHORIZED_MSG, position="top-right")
        return True, None

    @wraps(func)
    async def async_gen_wrapper(self: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        ok, event = await _check(self)
        if not ok:
            yield event
            return
        async for item in func(self, *args, **kwargs):
            yield item

    @wraps(func)
    async def async_wrapper(self: Any, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:
        ok, event = await _check(self)
        if not ok:
            return event
        return await func(self, *args, **kwargs)

    wrapper = async_gen_wrapper if inspect.isasyncgenfunction(func) else async_wrapper
    setattr(wrapper, ACCESS_LEVEL_ATTR, level)
    return wrapper  # type: ignore[return-value]


def requires_viewer[F: Callable[..., Any]](func: F) -> F:
    """Allow a read-only event for admins, project managers and employees."""
    return _guard(func, can_view, "viewer")


def requires_editor[F: Callable[..., Any]](func: F) -> F:
    """Allow a reading or writing event for admins and project managers."""
"""Permission roles of the alloq application (shared by app and components)."""

from alloq_commons.models.department import Department
from appkit_commons.roles import Role

PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE = Role(
    id=1,
    name="project_manager",
    label="Projektmanager",
    description="Voller Zugriff auf Planung, Projekte und Team, ohne Administration",
)

EMPLOYEE_ROLE = Role(
    id=2,
    name="employee",
    label="Mitarbeiter",
    description="Lesezugriff auf Projekte und Ressourcenplanung",
)

OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE = Role(
    id=3,
    name="offer_editor",
    label="Angebote",
    description="Lesen und Bearbeiten der Angebote",
)

ALL_ROLES: list[Role] = [
    PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE,
    EMPLOYEE_ROLE,
    OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE,
]

DEPARTMENT_ROLE_GROUP = "Abteilungen"


def department_role_name(department_id: int) -> str:
    """Permission role name of a department; keyed by id so renames keep it."""
    return f"department_{department_id}"


def department_roles(departments: list[Department]) -> list[Role]:
    """Permission roles offered in user management, one per department."""
    return [
        Role(
            name=department_role_name(d.id),
            label=d.label,
            description=f"Mitglied der Abteilung {d.name}",
            group=DEPARTMENT_ROLE_GROUP,
        )
        for d in departments
    ]

Yes. The only extra rule in the current code is the admin bypass, and your rules remove it. Without it, every check is just "does the user have role X". Nothing is changed yet.

**How it works today** ([access.py](components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/access.py)):

| Check | Today | Under your rules |
|---|---|---|
| Edit planning (`can_edit`, `CAN_EDIT`, `editor_only`, `@requires_editor`) | admin **or** project_manager | project_manager |
| Read planning (`can_view`, `CAN_VIEW`, `viewer_only`, `@requires_viewer`) | admin **or** project_manager **or** employee | project_manager **or** employee |
| Edit offers (`@requires_offer_editor`) | offer_editor | already done |
| Administration pages | appkit `requires_admin` | unchanged |

**What I would simplify:**

1. **Remove the admin switch from the planning checks.** `can_edit` becomes `PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE.name in user.roles`, and `CAN_EDIT` loses its `IS_ADMIN |` part. Read access follows automatically. The ~60 places that use `@requires_editor` / `editor_only` stay as they are, because the change is inside the helpers. This also covers `_can_edit` for the background dashboard loads in [dashboard_states.py:51](components/alloq-dashboard/src/alloq_dashboard/states/dashboard_states.py:51).
2. **Use one role-based guard instead of three.** `requires_viewer`, `requires_editor` and `requires_offer_editor` are the same code with a different check. They would become one factory, `requires_roles(*roles)`, plus three one-line names for it. The guard test then checks role names instead of the "viewer" / "editor" / "offer_editor" labels.
3. **Use appkit for the page-side checks where one role is enough.** `editor_only` becomes a thin wrapper around appkit's `requires_role(role=project_manager)`, the same tool the offers page uses now. `viewer_only` has to stay as a small helper of its own, because appkit's `requires_role` only checks a single role and reading allows two.
4. **Delete dead code.** The `admin_only()` component in access.py and `IS_ADMIN` are no longer used anywhere. The sidebar already uses appkit's `requires_admin`.

**One decision to make:** should a project manager also be able to read, or do they need the employee role on top? I'd say project manager includes reading. Otherwise someone could have edit rights but not see the pages to use them. If you choose the stricter version, every check becomes a single role, and `viewer_only` can also be replaced by appkit's `requires_role`.

**Risk:** admins who don't have the `project_manager` role will lose planning edit rights, and if they have no role at all, they'll lose read access too. That includes you. A small hand-written Alembic migration could give every current admin the `project_manager` role, so nobody gets locked out on deploy.

VERSIONS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "alembic" / "versions"

# Days after Easter Sunday for NRW's moveable holidays.
EASTER_OFFSETS = {
    "Karfreitag": -2,
    "Ostersonntag": 0,
    "Ostermontag": 1,
    "Christi Himmelfahrt": 39,
    "Pfingstsonntag": 49,
    "Pfingstmontag": 50,
    "Fronleichnam": 60,
}


def _easter(year: int) -> date:
    """Gregorian Easter Sunday (anonymous Gregorian algorithm)."""
    a = year % 19
    b, c = divmod(year, 100)
    d, e = divmod(b, 4)
    f = (b + 8) // 25
    g = (b - f + 1) // 3
    h = (19 * a + b - d - g + 15) % 30
    i, k = divmod(c, 4)
    l = (32 + 2 * e + 2 * i - h - k) % 7  # noqa: E741
    m = (a + 11 * h + 22 * l) // 451
    month, day = divmod(h + l - 7 * m + 114, 31)
    return date(year, month, day + 1)


def _load(filename: str) -> ModuleType:
    path = VERSIONS / filename
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(path.stem, path)
    assert spec is not None
    assert spec.loader is not None
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def seed_rows() -> list[dict]:
    """Rows the public_holidays migration bulk-inserts."""
    seed = _load("2026_05_11_public_holidays.py")
    fake_op = MagicMock()
    with patch.object(seed, "op", fake_op):
        seed.upgrade()
    return fake_op.bulk_insert.call_args.args[1]


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def fix() -> ModuleType:
    return _load("2026_09_28_fix_holiday_dates_and_default_admin.py")


@pytest.fixture
def connection(seed_rows: list[dict]) -> Iterator[Connection]:
    engine = sa.create_engine("sqlite://")
    metadata = sa.MetaData()
    holidays = sa.Table(
        "public_holidays",
        metadata,
        sa.Column("id", sa.Integer, primary_key=True),
        sa.Column("name", sa.String),
        sa.Column("date", sa.Date),
        sa.Column("is_recurring", sa.Boolean),
        sa.Column("state_code", sa.String),
    )
    sa.Table(
        "auth_users",
        metadata,
        sa.Column("id", sa.Integer, primary_key=True),
        sa.Column("email", sa.String),
        sa.Column("_password", sa.String),
        sa.Column("needs_password_reset", sa.Boolean),
    )
    with engine.begin() as conn:
        metadata.create_all(conn)
        conn.execute(holidays.insert(), seed_rows)
        yield conn


def _run(module: ModuleType, step: str, conn: Connection) -> None:
    operations = Operations(MigrationContext.configure(conn))
    with patch.object(module, "op", operations):
        getattr(module, step)()


def _holidays(conn: Connection) -> list[tuple[str, date]]:
    rows = conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT name, date FROM public_holidays"))
    return [(name, date.fromisoformat(str(day))) for name, day in rows]


def _moveable_mismatches(rows: list[tuple[str, date]]) -> list[tuple[str, date]]:
    return [
        (name, day)
        for name, day in rows
        if name in EASTER_OFFSETS
        and day != _easter(day.year) + timedelta(days=EASTER_OFFSETS[name])
    ]


def test_revision_chain(fix: ModuleType) -> None:
    seed = _load("2026_05_11_public_holidays.py")

    assert fix.down_revision == seed.revision


def test_department_highlight_migration_defaults_existing_rows_to_false() -> None:
    migration = _load("2026_10_19_department_highlight.py")
    engine = sa.create_engine("sqlite://")
    metadata = sa.MetaData()
    departments = sa.Table(
        "departments",
        metadata,
        sa.Column("id", sa.Integer, primary_key=True),
        sa.Column("name", sa.String, nullable=False),
    )
    with engine.begin() as conn:
        metadata.create_all(conn)
        conn.execute(departments.insert().values(name="IT"))
        _run(migration, "upgrade", conn)
        assert (
            conn.execute(sa.text("SELECT highlighted FROM departments")).scalar() == 0
        )
        conn.execute(sa.text("INSERT INTO departments (name) VALUES ('HR')"))
        assert (
            conn.execute(
                sa.text("SELECT highlighted FROM departments WHERE name = 'HR'")
            ).scalar()
            == 0
        )
        _run(migration, "downgrade", conn)
        columns = {
            column["name"] for column in sa.inspect(conn).get_columns("departments")
        }
        assert "highlighted" not in columns

class TestEmployeeRole:
    def test_employee_role_is_offered_in_user_management(self) -> None:
        assert EMPLOYEE_ROLE in ALL_ROLES
        assert EMPLOYEE_ROLE.name == "employee"
        assert len({role.name for role in ALL_ROLES}) == len(ALL_ROLES)


class TestCanView:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("user", "expected"),
        [(ADMIN, True), (MANAGER, True), (EMPLOYEE, True), (OTHER, False)],
    )
    def test_admins_managers_and_employees_may_read(
        self, user: User, expected: bool
    ) -> None:
        assert can_view(user) is expected


class TestCanEdit:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        ("user", "expected"),
        [(ADMIN, True), (MANAGER, True), (EMPLOYEE, False), (OTHER, False)],
    )
    def test_admins_and_project_managers_may_edit(
        self, user: User, expected: bool
    ) -> None:
        assert can_edit(user) is expected


class TestRequiresEditor:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("user", [ADMIN, MANAGER])
    async def test_admins_and_project_managers_run_the_handler(
        self, user: User
    ) -> None:
        editor = _Editor(user)
        assert await editor.save(3) == 4
        assert await _collect(editor.save_stream()) == ["saved"]
        assert editor.calls == 2

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("user", [EMPLOYEE, OTHER])
    async def test_readers_and_others_are_denied(self, user: User) -> None:
        editor = _Editor(user)
        assert await editor.save(3) is not None
        assert len(await _collect(editor.save_stream())) == 1
        assert editor.calls == 0

    async def test_anonymous_users_are_redirected(self) -> None:
        editor = _Editor(None)
        assert await editor.save(3) == "redirect"
        assert editor.login.redirected
        assert editor.calls == 0

    def test_keeps_the_handler_name(self) -> None:
        assert _Editor.save.__name__ == "save"


class TestRequiresViewer:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("user", [ADMIN, MANAGER, EMPLOYEE])
    async def test_allowed_users_run_the_handler(self, user: User) -> None:
        reader = _Reader(user)
        assert await reader.read(3) == 6
        assert await _collect(reader.stream()) == ["loaded"]
        assert reader.calls == 2

    async def test_other_users_get_an_error_and_the_handler_does_not_run(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        reader = _Reader(OTHER)
        result = await reader.read(3)
        events = await _collect(reader.stream())
        assert reader.calls == 0
        assert result is not None
        assert len(events) == 1
        assert events[0] is not None

    async def test_anonymous_users_are_redirected(self) -> None:
        reader = _Reader(None)
        assert await reader.read(3) == "redirect"
        assert await _collect(reader.stream()) == ["redirect"]
        assert reader.login.redirected
        assert reader.calls == 0

    async def test_denial_is_not_mistaken_for_access_when_redirect_is_none(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        reader = _Reader(None)
        reader.login.redir = AsyncMock(return_value=None)  # ty: ignore[invalid-assignment]
        assert await reader.read(3) is None
        assert reader.calls == 0

    def test_keeps_the_handler_name(self) -> None:
        assert _Reader.read.__name__ == "read"


class TestRenderGuards:
    def test_viewer_only_checks_admin_or_employee_role(self) -> None:
        rendered = str(viewer_only(rx.text("x")))
        assert "is_admin" in rendered
        assert EMPLOYEE_ROLE.name in rendered

    def test_admin_only_checks_admin_flag(self) -> None:
        rendered = str(admin_only(rx.text("x")))
        assert "is_admin" in rendered
        assert EMPLOYEE_ROLE.name not in rendered
        assert PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE.name not in rendered

    def test_editor_only_checks_admin_or_project_manager_role(self) -> None:
        rendered = str(editor_only(rx.text("x")))
        assert "is_admin" in rendered
        assert PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE.name in rendered
        assert EMPLOYEE_ROLE.name not in rendered

    def test_viewer_only_includes_project_managers(self) -> None:
        assert PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE.name in str(CAN_VIEW)
        assert PROJECT_MANAGER_ROLE.name in str(CAN_EDIT)

    def test_can_view_includes_admin_flag_and_role(self) -> None:
        assert "is_admin" in str(CAN_VIEW)
        assert EMPLOYEE_ROLE.name in str(CAN_VIEW)
        assert "is_admin" in str(IS_ADMIN)

    def test_no_access_explains_the_missing_rights(self) -> None:
        # Reflex escapes umlauts on render; the message has none up to here.
        assert NO_ACCESS_MSG.split(",")[0] in str(no_access())

    def test_fallback_is_rendered(self) -> None:
        rendered = str(viewer_only(rx.text("inside"), fallback=rx.text("outside")))
            (OFFER_EDITOR, True),
            (EMPLOYEE, False),
            (OTHER, False),
            (NO_ROLES, False),
        ],
    )
    def test_can_edit_offers(self, user: User, expected: bool) -> None:
        assert can_edit_offers(user) is expected

    def test_offer_editor_gets_no_planning_access(self) -> None:
        assert can_edit(OFFER_EDITOR) is False
        assert can_view(OFFER_EDITOR) is False

    async def test_offer_editors_run_the_handler(self) -> None:
        editor = _OfferEditor(OFFER_EDITOR)

Access now depends on roles alone: the admin switch opens only the
administration, and a project manager needs the employee role to read the
planning. So nobody loses access on deploy, every admin gets the
``project_manager`` and ``employee`` roles, and every project manager gets the
``employee`` role.

Revision ID: e023b4c5d6f7
Revises: df12a3b4c5e6
Create Date: 2026-10-21 18:00:00.000000

"""

import sqlalchemy as sa
from appkit_commons.database.entities import ArrayType

from alembic import op

branch_labels: str | Sequence[str] | None = None

EMPLOYEE = "employee"

_users = sa.table(
    "auth_users",
    sa.column("id", sa.Integer),
    sa.column("is_admin", sa.Boolean),
    sa.column("roles", ArrayType()),
)


def granted_roles(roles: list[str], *, is_admin: bool) -> list[str]:
    """``roles`` plus the roles the old admin/manager rules implied."""
    added = []
    if is_admin:
        added.append(PROJECT_MANAGER)
    if is_admin or PROJECT_MANAGER in roles:
        added.append(EMPLOYEE)
    return [*roles, *(role for role in added if role not in roles)]


def upgrade() -> None:
    bind = op.get_bind()
    rows = bind.execute(sa.select(_users.c.id, _users.c.is_admin, _users.c.roles))
    for user_id, is_admin, roles in rows.all():
        current = list(roles or [])
        updated = granted_roles(current, is_admin=bool(is_admin))
        if updated != current:
            bind.execute(
                _users.update().where(_users.c.id == user_id).values(roles=updated)
            )


def downgrade() -> None:
    # The granted roles stay: the old rules already gave admins and project
    # managers this access, and removing them could drop roles set by hand.
    pass

---
name: employee-role-read-only
description: Alloq access is role-only: admin switch = administration only; employee reads planning, project_manager edits (needs employee on top)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Since 2026-10-21 access in `alloq_commons.access` depends on roles alone; roles add up:
- Admin (`is_admin` switch): only the administration pages (users, roles, departments, holidays, daily rates, DB access) via `@requires_admin` / appkit `requires_admin` / `app_page(admin_only=True)`. It grants no planning or offer access.
- `employee` role: reads /plan and /projects (`@requires_viewer` + `VIEWER_HANDLERS`, `viewer_only`).

content.text:
Planning access now depends only on roles. Format, lint, typecheck and the full test suite pass (1556 tests, 10 s). Nothing is committed, and I didn't check it in the running app.

About the test hang: it wasn't a bug in the app. The dashboard tests used a fake admin with no roles. Its background load was then refused, and the test kept waiting for data that never came. All the allowed test users now get the `project_manager` and `employee` roles, so no test hangs any more.

**The new rules in [access.py](components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/access.py):**
- **`employee`** can read /plan and /projects (`@requires_viewer`, `viewer_only`).
- **`project_manager`** can edit, and can open the dashboard and team pages (`@requires_editor`, `editor_only`, `CAN_EDIT`). To read /plan and /projects, a project manager also needs the `employee` role.
- **The admin switch** only opens administration. It grants nothing else.

**Simplified code:**
- **One server check:** `has_role(user, role)` handles every check. The three guards are one-liners on top of it, and the background dashboard loads use the same check.
- **Page-side guards:** `editor_only` and `viewer_only` now wrap appkit's `requires_role`.
- **Removed:** `IS_ADMIN`, `CAN_VIEW`, `admin_only()`, `can_edit`, `can_view` and `can_edit_offers`.

**Migration** [2026_10_21_role_only_access.py](alembic/versions/2026_10_21_role_only_access.py) (`e023b4c5d6f7`):
- **Admins** get `project_manager` and `employee`.
- **Project managers** get `employee`.
- **Roles already set** stay as they are.
- **It works on both PostgreSQL and SQLite.** A test runs it on SQLite.
- **It's registered** in `KNOWN_REVISIONS`.
- **`downgrade()` does nothing on purpose.** Taking the roles away again could remove roles someone set by hand.

One test, [test_index_migration.py](tests/test_index_migration.py), required the index migration to be the newest one. It now only checks that the index migration is a known revision.

**Watch out:** someone else is working in this checkout right now. Two new commits are on `main` (the Gantt cleanup and the planned-days fix), and a "discard changes" feature is staged. That staging also picked up three of my files: `access.py`, `test_access.py` and `dashboard_states.py`. A commit made from the index as it is would mix both pieces of work.
